source.title: Open Problems in Geometry and Topology

accepted.question_text: Let M be a closed, connected, oriented, irreducible 3-manifold. Must exactly one of the following alternatives hold: (a) M is isometric to a quotient S^3/Γ of the round 3-sphere by a subgroup Γ of Isom(S^3); (b) the fundamental group π1(M) contains a subgroup isomorphic to Z ⊕ Z; or (c) M is isometric to a quotient H^3/Γ of hyperbolic 3-space by a subgroup Γ of Isom(H^3)?

evidence.quote: Thurston's Geometrization Conjecture: Let M be a closed, connected, oriented, irreducible 3-manifold. Then precisely one of the following holds: a) M = S^3/Γ, where Γ ⊂ Isom(S^3). b) Z ⊕ Z ⊂ π1(M). c) M = H^3/Γ, where Γ ⊂ Isom(H^3).

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a knot in the 3-sphere S^3, distinct from the unknot, whose Jones polynomial is equal to the Jones polynomial of the unknot?
accepted.context_brief: Jones polynomial detection of the unknot

evidence.quote: Does there exist another knot in the 3-sphere with the same Jones polynomial as the unknot?

accepted.question_text: Fix an integer n ≥ 1. A generalized knot in S^3 is an oriented immersed circle with only double-point self-intersections, such that the two tangent vectors at each double point are distinct. Let I be an ambient-isotopy invariant of generalized knots in S^3 with at least n double points, and suppose that I integrates to an invariant of generalized knots with n−1 double points in the following sense: there exists an invariant I′ of generalized knots with n−1 double points such that I(K) = Σ_{p∈D}(I′(K^+_p) − I′(K^-_p)), where D is the set of double points of K, K^+_p is obtained by resolving the double point p into one crossing, and K^-_p is obtained by resolving the same double point into the opposite crossing. Must I then integrate all the way to an invariant of honest knots?

evidence.quote: A generalized knot in S^3 is an oriented, immersed circle with only double point self intersections, and where the two tangent vectors to each double point are distinct. Now, let I denote and ambient, isotopy invariant of generalized knots in S^3 with at least n double points. Suppose that I integrates to an invariant of generalized knots with

n − 1 double points. Does I then integrate to an invariant of honest knots? Note that an invariant, I, immersed circles with n double points is said to integrate to an invariant of circles with n − 1 double points when there exists and invariant of the latter, I′, with the property that I(K) = Σ_{p∈D}(I′(K^+_p) − I′(K^-_p)). Here, the sum is over the set D of double points of K; and K^+_p and K^-_p are the generalized knots with n−1 double points which are obtained from K as follows: First, view K so that a neighbourhood of p in K looks like and x with both branches oriented to point towards the top of the page. Then, K^+_p is obtained by resolving the cross with the branch/passing over the other branch. Meanwhile, K^-_p is obtained by resolving the double point using the opposite crossing.

accepted.question_text: Is the smooth 4-dimensional Poincaré conjecture true? Equivalently, if X is a compact 4-manifold with vanishing π1(X) and π2(X), must X be diffeomorphic to the 4-sphere S^4?

evidence.quote: Is the smooth, 4-dimensional Poincare conjecture true? That is, if a compact, 4-dimensional manifold has vanishing π1 and π2, is it necessary diffeomorphic to S^4?

accepted.question_text: For an integer k > 2, let X be a smooth, compact manifold of real dimension 2k that admits an almost complex structure. Must X admit some complex-manifold structure, not necessarily homotopic to the given almost complex structure?

evidence.quote: If k > 2, does every smooth, compact, 2k-dimensional manifold which admits an almost complex structure have the structure of a complex manifold? (The almost complex structure as a complex manifold need not to be homotopic to the given one.)

accepted.question_text: Let X be a smooth projective variety. Let Hol(X,BU)^+ denote the Quillen-Segal group completion of the holomorphic mapping space from X to BU, where BU is viewed as the union of Grassmannians, so that holomorphic maps X → BU classify holomorphic vector bundles over X that are holomorphically embedded in trivial bundles. Under what conditions on X is the natural inclusion Hol(X,BU)^+ → Maps(X,BU) a homotopy equivalence?

evidence.quote: Let X be a smooth, projective variety and consider the Quillen-Segal group completion of the holomorphic mapping space, Hol(X,BU)^+, where BU is viewed as a union of Grassmannians. This space represents the "holomorphic K-theory" of X in that holomorphic maps from X to BU classify holomorphic vector bundles over X that are holomorphically embedded in trivial bundles. It is known that this

theory satisfies a kind of periodicity and sits between algebraic K-theory on the one hand and topological K-theory on the other. With the preceding understood, under what conditions (on X) is the inclusion Hol(X,BU)^+ → Maps(X,BU) a homotopy equivalence?

accepted.question_text: Let X be a simply connected finite CW complex. Suppose the rational homotopy groups are finite-dimensional in the sense that dim(π_*(X) ⊗ Q) is finite. For each prime p, does there exist an integer k such that multiplication by p^k annihilates the p-torsion in π_*(X)?
accepted.context_brief: Moore conjecture on p-torsion in homotopy groups

evidence.quote: The following is a question asked by John Moore about homotopy groups: Suppose that X is a simply connected, finite complex. If dim(π*(X) ⊗ Q) is finite, is there, for each prime p, and integer k for which p^k annihilates the p-torsion in π*(X)?

accepted.question_text: For a closed oriented surface of genus g ≥ 2, does its mapping class group satisfy Kazhdan's Property T?
accepted.context_brief: mapping class groups and Property T

evidence.quote: Does the mapping class group of a surface of genus g ≥ 2 satisfy Kazhdan's Property T?

accepted.question_text: Let π be a Poincaré duality group, meaning that the Eilenberg-MacLane space K(π,1) satisfies Poincaré duality with respect to a fundamental class in H^n(K(π,1); Z) for some n. Is K(π,1) simple-homotopy equivalent to a closed topological manifold, and if so is that manifold unique up to homeomorphism?
accepted.context_brief: Borel-type conjecture for Poincaré duality groups

evidence.quote: Let π be a Poincare duality group. That is, the Eilenberg-MacLane space K(π,1) satisfies Poincare duality with respect to a fundamental class in H^n(K;Z) for some n. Prove or disprove the "Borel conjecture": K(π,1) is simple homotopy equivalent to a closed, topological m-manifold which is unique up to homeomorphism.

accepted.question_text: Does the 4-sphere S^4 carry a unique Einstein metric up to diffeomorphism?

evidence.quote: Settle the Euclidean no hair question: Does the four dimensional sphere have a unique Einstein metric (up to diffeomorphism)?
